title: Bipartite (k1,k2,l)-sparsity is equivalent to arboricity of the associated butterfly multigraph after adding l-1 edges
author: Signe Lundqvist; Tovohery Randrianarisoa; Klara Stokes; Joannes Vermant
work: Sparsity greedoids and pebble game algorithms for posets
difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the bipartite sparsity/arboricity equivalence of source lines 196-199, in which the auxiliary object is the (k1,k2)-fold butterfly multigraph of the bipartite graph and the hypothesis is that one may add any l-1 edges between the two sides. The work is entirely in the two counting chains at 201-202 and 208-213: the first has to convert a forest-decomposition bound of the butterfly graph into the sparsity inequality of the bipartite graph while carrying the (l-1)k1k2 added edges, and the second has to sum the per-copy sparsity bounds over all k1k2 vertex-class pairs to reach the Nash-Williams form. Neither direction is a direct restatement of the cited Nash-Williams theorem, and the butterfly construction itself is defined at 194.
